frase_gancho.texto: Heirs of the maguey: textiles, fibers, and altars of the peoples of the highlands.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: The Otopame Peoples are a group of peoples who speak related languages: Otomí, Mazahua, Matlatzinca, Pame, and others. They live mostly in the Central Highlands, among cold valleys, mountains, and semideserts such as the Valle del Mezquital, in Hidalgo. They are thought to be among the oldest inhabitants of the region, predating the Mexica. Here the most important plant is the maguey, which provides fiber, food, drink, roofing, and even needle and thread. The Hall shows you how, with that resource, with the wool of sheep, and with a faith that blends saints and hills, these peoples built a world of their own, made of textiles, fibers, and altars.
